subject: gk
question: In August 2025, Assam has launched the Operation Falcon ___________.

options.text: to protect one-horned rhinos from poachers
to deport illegal migrants from Bangladesh to their country
to tackle naxalism in the state
to tackle leakages in direct benefit transfer

solution:
The correct answer is __**to protect one-horned rhinos from poachers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Operation Falcon** was launched by the Assam government in **August 2025** to address the critical issue of poaching of one-horned rhinos in the state.

• The state of Assam is globally renowned for its **Kaziranga National Park**, which houses the majority of the world's population of **Indian one-horned rhinos**.

• The operation aims to strengthen anti-poaching measures by deploying **advanced surveillance technology**, increasing manpower, and intensifying security protocols in rhino habitats.

• One-horned rhinos are classified as **vulnerable** under the **IUCN Red List**, and their conservation is critical for maintaining biodiversity.

• Rhino poaching is primarily driven by the **illegal trade of rhino horns**, which are falsely believed to have medicinal properties in certain cultures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **One-Horned Rhino Conservation Efforts:**

• The **Indian one-horned rhinoceros**, also known as the **Indian rhinoceros**, is primarily found in Assam, particularly in **Kaziranga National Park**, Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary, and Manas National Park.

• Conservation efforts have included the **Indian Rhino Vision 2020**, which aimed to increase the population of rhinos to 3,000 by 2020 across protected areas in Assam.

• Efforts like **anti-poaching camps**, community awareness programs, and strict enforcement of wildlife laws have been implemented.

• Technology such as **drones and GPS tracking** has been increasingly employed for surveillance and monitoring of rhino habitats.

• **Illegal Trade and Threats:**

• Rhino horns are often trafficked in international markets, particularly in **Asia**, where they are falsely believed to have medicinal properties.

• The horns are composed primarily of **keratin**, the same substance found in human hair and nails, and have no proven medicinal value.

• Poaching, habitat loss, and human-wildlife conflict are the primary threats to rhino populations.

• **Indian Wildlife Protection Framework:**

• The conservation of rhinos is supported under the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**, which prohibits hunting and trade of endangered species.

• The **National Board for Wildlife** and various state wildlife boards actively work toward the protection of endangered species.

• **Kaziranga National Park:**

• Kaziranga National Park is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** located in Assam, famous for its population of one-horned rhinos.

• The park spans an area of approximately **430 square kilometers** and includes grasslands, wetlands, and tropical forests.

• Kaziranga has been a success story in rhino conservation, with the rhino population increasing due to stringent anti-poaching measures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Other Conservation Programs:**

• The **Project Tiger** and **Project Elephant** are similar initiatives aimed at conserving other endangered species in India.

• Community participation plays a vital role in wildlife conservation. Programs like the **Eco-development Committees** engage local communities in conservation efforts.

• **International Agreements:**

• India is a signatory to the **Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES)**, which regulates trade in endangered species.

• Collaborative efforts with neighboring countries such as **Nepal** and **Bhutan** have been undertaken for transboundary conservation.

• **Threatened Species in India:**

• Other vulnerable species in India include the **Bengal tiger, Asiatic lion, and Indian elephant**, which are also subject to conservation initiatives.
